notes: §1985:XII.2.3 SR2: 'The COPY statement must be preceded by a space and terminated by the separator period.' CopyProcessor#FindStatementKeyword (from ExpandCopiesOneLevel) reports a COPY glued behind a period, comma or semicolon and ResolveOneCopy reports one directly after a parenthesis, colon or literal delimiter (COBOL2451); ParseCopyStatement ends the statement through StatementCursor's ExpectSeparatorPeriod (COBOL2449), at every edition. The 2023 exception for the first statement of a compilation group (copyIdx 0) is not reached by 1985 reference format, where column 8 follows the indicator area. Probes at 85: COPY PDTEXT. and 'DISPLAY "A". COPY PDTEXT.' run; '"A".COPY', '"A"COPY', 'TE(COPY ONE.)' refused COBOL2451; COPY with no period, with a comma, and REPLACING with no period refused COBOL2449; 'COPY PDTEXT..' refused (CBL3620 on the name 'PDTEXT.'). Under the non-1985 --source-format free a COPY at column 1 of line 1 is accepted. The witness is 'COPY PDTEXT DISPLAY ...' (no period).

next.reason: 1985: 'The COPY statement must be preceded by a space and terminated by the separator period', with no exception. §2023:7.2.3.3 SR2: 'A COPY statement shall be preceded by a space except when it is the first statement in a compilation group' - a case 1985 refused is accepted. The terminating period is kept: the format §2023:7.2.3.2 ends with it and §2023:7.2.3.4 GR6 replaces the statement 'ending with the separator period, inclusive'. Looser.
